1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle (sent one), separated (set apart) to the gospel (good news) of God,
Which God had promised before by His prophets in the holy scriptures,
About His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, who was made of the seed (family line) of David according to the flesh (as a man),
And declared (shown) to be the Son of God with power, according to the Spirit of holiness, by the resurrection (rising) from the dead.
By Him we have received grace and apostleship (the work of an apostle), for obedience to the faith among all nations, for His name.
Among them are you also the called of Jesus Christ.
To all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints (holy people): Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel (good news) of His Son, that without ceasing (stopping) I make mention of you always in my prayers,
Making request, if by any means now at last I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come to you.
For I long to see you, that I may give to you some spiritual gift, to the end you may be established (made strong).
That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual (shared) faith both of you and me.

Now I would not have you ignorant (not knowing), brothers, that often I purposed (planned) to come to you, but was let (stopped) until now. I wanted to have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
I am debtor (I owe the gospel) both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians (people who did not speak Greek), both to the wise, and to the unwise.
So, as much as is in me, I am ready to preach the gospel (good news) to you who are at Rome also.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel (good news) of Christ. For it is the power of God unto salvation to every one who believes, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
For in it is the righteousness (being right with God) of God revealed (shown) from faith to faith. As it is written: The just (those who are right with God) will live by faith.
For the wrath (God's anger) of God is revealed (shown) from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness (wrong) of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness (wrong).
Because that which may be known of God is manifest (clear) in them. For God has shown it to them.

For the invisible things of God are clearly seen from the creation of the world. They are understood by the things that are made. Even His eternal power and Godhead (that He is God) are seen. So they are without excuse.
Because, when they knew God, they glorified (praised) Him not as God, neither were thankful. But they became vain (empty) in their imaginations (thoughts), and their foolish heart was darkened.
Professing (claiming) themselves to be wise, they became fools,
And changed the glory of the uncorruptible (never decaying) God into an image made like to corruptible (decaying) man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts (animals with 4 legs), and creeping things.
So God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts (wrong desires) of their own hearts, to dishonor their own bodies between themselves.
They changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature (what God made) more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.
For this cause God gave them up to vile affections (shameful desires). For even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature.

And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust (wrong desire) one toward another, men with men working that which is unseemly (shameful). They received in themselves that recompence (payment) of their error which was meet (deserved).
Even as they did not like to retain (keep) God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate (worthless, rejected) mind, to do those things which are not convenient (right).

They were filled with all unrighteousness (wrong), fornication (sexual sin), wickedness, covetousness (wanting what belongs to others), maliciousness (wanting to hurt others). They were full of envy (jealousy), murder, debate (fighting), deceit (lying), malignity (evil thoughts). They were whisperers (gossips),
Backbiters (people who speak evil of others), haters of God, despiteful (insulting), proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
Without understanding, agreement breakers (people who break their promises), without natural affection (love), implacable (refusing to make peace), unmerciful.
They know the judgment of God, that those who commit such things are worthy of death. Yet they not only do the same, but have pleasure in (approve of) those who do them.

2.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: So you are inexcusable (have no excuse), O man, whoever you are who judges. For in the thing in which you judge another, you condemn (judge guilty) yourself. For you who judge do the same things.
But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against those who commit such things.
And do you think this, O man, who judges those who do such things, and does the same, that you will escape the judgment of God?

Or do you despise (look down on) the riches of His goodness and forbearance (patience) and longsuffering (waiting a long time)? Do you not know that the goodness of God leads you to repentance (a change of heart)?

But after your hardness and impenitent (unchanged) heart you treasure up (store up) to yourself wrath (God's anger) against the day of wrath (God's anger) and revelation (showing) of the righteous (right) judgment of God,
Who will render (give) to every man according to his deeds:
To those who by patient continuance (keeping on) in well doing seek for glory and honor and immortality (life that never dies), eternal life.
But to those who are contentious (fighting), and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness (wrong), God will give indignation (anger) and wrath (God's anger),
Tribulation (trouble) and anguish (deep pain), upon every soul of man who does evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile (person who is not a Jew).
But glory, honor, and peace, to every man who works good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile (person who is not a Jew).
For there is no respect of persons with God (God does not show favor to some people over others).
For as many as have sinned without law will also perish (be destroyed) without law. And as many as have sinned in the law will be judged by the law.
For not the hearers of the law are just (right with God) before God, but the doers of the law will be justified (made right with God).
For when the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), who do not have the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves.
They show the work of the law written in their hearts. Their conscience also bears witness, and their thoughts the mean while accuse or else excuse one another.
In the day when God will judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel (good news).
Look, you are called a Jew, and rest in the law, and make your boast (brag) of God,
And know His will, and approve the things that are more excellent, being instructed (taught) out of the law.
You are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of those who are in darkness,
An instructor (teacher) of the foolish, a teacher of babes (little children), which have the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
So you who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach that a man should not steal, do you steal?
You who say a man should not commit adultery (sex outside marriage), do you commit adultery? You who abhor (hate) idols, do you commit sacrilege (rob what is holy)?
You who make your boast (brag) of the law, through breaking the law do you dishonor God?
For the name of God is blasphemed (spoken against) among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) through you, as it is written.
For circumcision (cutting off the foreskin) truly profits (helps), if you keep the law. But if you are a breaker of the law, your circumcision is made uncircumcision.
So if the uncircumcision (people who are not circumcised) keep the righteousness (right rules) of the law, will not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
And will not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge you, who by the letter and circumcision do break the law?
For he is not a Jew, who is one outwardly. Neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh.
But he is a Jew, who is one inwardly. And circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter. His praise is not of men, but of God.

3.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: What advantage then has the Jew? Or what profit (help) is there of circumcision (cutting off the foreskin)?
Much every way. Chiefly, because to them were committed (given) the oracles (words) of God.
For what if some did not believe? Will their unbelief make the faith (faithfulness) of God without effect?
God forbid (no, never). Yes, let God be true, but every man a liar. As it is written: That You might be justified (shown to be right) in Your sayings, and might overcome when You are judged.
But if our unrighteousness (wrong) commend (shows) the righteousness (rightness) of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous (wrong) who takes vengeance (pays back)? (I speak as a man.)
God forbid (no, never). For then how will God judge the world?
For if the truth of God has more abounded (grown) through my lie to His glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
And not rather, as we are slanderously reported (lied about), and as some affirm (claim) that we say: Let us do evil, that good may come? Their damnation (being condemned) is just (fair).
What then? Are we better than they? No, in no way. For we have before proved both Jews and Gentiles (people who are not Jews), that they are all under sin.
As it is written: There is none righteous (right with God), no, not one.
There is none who understands. There is none who seeks after God.
They have all gone out of the way. They have together become unprofitable (worthless). There is none who does good, no, not one.
Their throat is an open sepulchre (tomb). With their tongues they have used deceit (lies). The poison of asps (snakes) is under their lips.
Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
Their feet are swift (fast) to shed blood.
Destruction and misery are in their ways.
And the way of peace they have not known.
There is no fear of God before their eyes.
Now we know that what things soever (whatever) the law says, it says to those who are under the law. So every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God.
So by the deeds of the law there will no flesh (no person) be justified (made right with God) in His sight. For by the law is the knowledge of sin.
But now the righteousness (being right with God) of God without the law is manifested (shown), being witnessed by the law and the prophets.
Even the righteousness (being right with God) of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all those who believe. For there is no difference.
For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God.
Being justified (made right with God) freely by His grace through the redemption (being bought back and set free) that is in Christ Jesus.

God has set forth Jesus to be a propitiation (the sacrifice that turns away God's anger) through faith in His blood, to declare (show) His righteousness (rightness) for the remission (forgiveness) of sins that are past, through the forbearance (patience) of God.
To declare (show), I say, at this time His righteousness (rightness), so that He might be just (right), and the justifier (the one who makes right with God) of the one who believes in Jesus.
Where is boasting (bragging) then? It is excluded (shut out). By what law? Of works? No. But by the law of faith.
So we conclude that a man is justified (made right with God) by faith without the deeds of the law.
Is He the God of the Jews only? Is He not also of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews)? Yes, of the Gentiles also.
Seeing it is one God, who will justify (make right with God) the circumcision (Jews) by faith, and uncircumcision (people who are not Jews) through faith.
Do we then make void (empty) the law through faith? God forbid (no, never). Yes, we establish (make firm) the law.

verses.text: What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to (about) the flesh, has found?
For if Abraham were justified (made right with God) by works (the good things we do), he has something to glory (brag) about, but not before God.
For what does the scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness (being right with God).
Now to the one who works is the reward not reckoned (counted) of grace, but of debt (what is owed).
But to the one who does not work, but believes on Him who justifies (makes right with God) the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness (being right with God).
Even as David also describes the blessedness of the man, to whom God imputes (counts) righteousness (being right with God) without works,
Saying: Blessed are those whose iniquities (sins) are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute (count) sin.

Comes this blessedness then upon the circumcision (Jews) only, or upon the uncircumcision (people who are not Jews) also? For we say that faith was reckoned (counted) to Abraham for righteousness (being right with God).
How was it then reckoned (counted)? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

Abraham received the sign of circumcision (cutting off the foreskin), a seal of the righteousness (being right with God) of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised. So he might be the father of all those who believe, though they are not circumcised, that righteousness might be imputed (counted) to them also.
And the father of circumcision to those who are not of the circumcision only, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham, which he had being yet uncircumcised.
For the promise, that he should be the heir of the world, was not to Abraham, or to his seed (family line), through the law, but through the righteousness (being right with God) of faith.
For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith is made void (empty), and the promise made of none effect (useless).
Because the law works wrath (God's anger). For where no law is, there is no transgression (breaking of the law).

So it is of faith, that it might be by grace. Then the promise might be sure to all the seed (family line). Not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,

As it is written: I have made you a father of many nations. This was before Him whom he believed, even God, who quickens (makes alive) the dead, and calls those things which are not as though they were.
Who against hope believed in hope, that he might become the father of many nations, according to that which was spoken: So will your seed (family line) be.
Being not weak in faith, Abraham considered not his own body now dead, when he was about 100 years old, neither yet the deadness of Sara's (Sarah's) womb.
He staggered not (did not doubt) at the promise of God through unbelief. But he was strong in faith, giving glory to God.
Being fully persuaded (sure) that, what God had promised, He was able also to perform (do).
And so it was imputed (counted) to him for righteousness (being right with God).
Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was imputed (counted) to him.
But for us also, to whom it will be imputed (counted), if we believe on Him who raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead.
Jesus was delivered (handed over to death) for our offences (sins), and was raised again for our justification (being made right with God).

5.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: So being justified (made right with God) by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
By Him also we have access (a way in) by faith into this grace in which we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
And not only so, but we glory (rejoice) in tribulations (troubles) also, knowing that tribulation (trouble) works patience,
And patience, experience (proven character). And experience (proven character), hope.
And hope makes not ashamed, because the love of God is shed abroad (poured out) in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who is given to us.
For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.
For scarcely (hardly) for a righteous (good) man will one die. Yet perhaps for a good man some would even dare to die.
But God commends (shows) His love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
Much more then, being now justified (made right with God) by His blood, we will be saved from wrath (God's anger) through Him.
For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled (brought back) to God by the death of His Son, much more, being reconciled, we will be saved by His life.
And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement (being made one with God again).
So, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin, so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.
For until the law sin was in the world. But sin is not imputed (counted) when there is no law.

Nevertheless death reigned (ruled) from Adam to Moses, even over those who had not sinned after the likeness (looking like) of Adam's transgression (breaking of the law), who is the figure (picture) of Him who was to come.

But not as the offence (sin), so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many are dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, has abounded (overflowed) to many.

And not as it was by one who sinned, so is the gift. For the judgment was by one to condemnation (being judged guilty), but the free gift is of many offences (sins) unto justification (being made right with God).

For if by one man's offence (sin) death reigned (ruled) by one, much more those who receive abundance (much) of grace and of the gift of righteousness (being right with God) will reign (rule) in life by one, Jesus Christ.

So as by the offence (sin) of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation (being judged guilty), even so by the righteousness (right act) of one the free gift came upon all men unto justification (being made right with God) of life.
For as by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one will many be made righteous (right with God).
Moreover the law entered, that the offence (sin) might abound (grow). But where sin abounded (grew), grace did much more abound (overflow).
That as sin has reigned (ruled) unto death, even so might grace reign (rule) through righteousness (being right with God) unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound (grow)?
God forbid (no, never). How shall we, who are dead to sin, live any longer in it?
Do you not know, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into His death?
So we are buried with Him by baptism into death. Like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
For if we have been planted together in the likeness (looking like) of His death, we will be also in the likeness of His resurrection (rising).
Knowing this, that our old man (old self) is crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be destroyed. So from now on we should not serve sin.
For the one who is dead is freed from sin.
Now if we are dead with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
Knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dies no more. Death has no more dominion (rule) over Him.
For in that He died, He died unto sin once. But in that He lives, He lives unto God.
Likewise reckon (count) yourselves also to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
So do not let sin reign (rule) in your mortal (that will die) body, that you should obey it in the lusts (wrong desires) of it.

Neither yield (give) your members (body parts) as instruments of unrighteousness (wrong) unto sin. But yield yourselves to God, as those who are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness (what is right) to God.
For sin will not have dominion (rule) over you. For you are not under the law, but under grace.
What then? Shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid (no, never).
Do you not know, that to whom you yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants you are to whom you obey? Whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness (being right with God)?
But God be thanked, that you were the servants of sin, but you have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine (teaching) which was delivered (given) to you.
Being then made free from sin, you became the servants of righteousness (what is right).

I speak after the manner of men because of the infirmity (weakness) of your flesh. For as you have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity (sin) unto iniquity, even so now yield your members servants to righteousness (what is right) unto holiness.
For when you were the servants of sin, you were free from righteousness (what is right).
What fruit had you then in those things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, you have your fruit unto holiness, and the end everlasting life.
For the wages (payment) of sin is death. But the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Do you not know, brothers (for I speak to those who know the law), that the law has dominion (rule) over a man as long as he lives?
For the woman who has a husband is bound by the law to her husband as long as he lives. But if the husband is dead, she is loosed (set free) from the law of her husband.

So then if, while her husband lives, she is married to another man, she will be called an adulteress (a woman who has sex outside marriage). But if her husband is dead, she is free from that law. So she is no adulteress, though she is married to another man.
So, my brothers, you also have become dead to the law by the body of Christ. So you should be married to Another, even to Him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God.
For when we were in the flesh (sinful self), the motions (desires) of sins, which were by the law, worked in our members (body parts) to bring forth fruit unto death.
But now we are delivered (set free) from the law, that being dead in which we were held. So we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.

What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid (no, never). No, I had not known sin, but by the law. For I had not known lust (wrong desire), except the law had said: You will not covet (want what belongs to others).
But sin, taking occasion (a chance) by the commandment, worked in me all manner of concupiscence (wrong desire). For without the law sin was dead.
For I was alive without the law once. But when the commandment came, sin revived (came alive), and I died.
The commandment, which was ordained (meant) to life, I found to be unto death.
For sin, taking occasion (a chance) by the commandment, deceived (tricked) me, and by it killed me.
So the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just (fair), and good.

Was then that which is good made death to me? God forbid (no, never). But sin, that it might appear sin, worked death in me by that which is good. So sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.
For we know that the law is spiritual. But I am carnal (ruled by the sinful self), sold under sin.
For that which I do I allow (understand) not. For what I would (want to do), that I do not do. But what I hate, that I do.
If then I do that which I would not (do not want to do), I consent (agree) to the law that it is good.
Now then it is no more I who do it, but sin that dwells (lives) in me.
For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh) dwells (lives) no good thing. For to will (want) is present with me. But how to perform (do) that which is good I do not find.
For the good that I would (want to do) I do not do. But the evil which I would not (do not want to do), that I do.
Now if I do that which I would not (do not want to do), it is no more I who do it, but sin that dwells (lives) in me.
I find then a law, that, when I would (want to) do good, evil is present with me.
For I delight in the law of God after the inward man (my inner self).
But I see another law in my members (body parts), warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity (prison) to the law of sin which is in my members.
O wretched (miserable) man that I am. Who will deliver (rescue) me from the body of this death?
I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God, but with the flesh (sinful self) the law of sin.

8.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: There is therefore now no condemnation (being judged guilty) to those who are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh (sinful self), but after the Spirit.
For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the law of sin and death.

For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh (sinful self), God sending His own Son in the likeness (looking like) of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned (judged guilty) sin in the flesh.
So the righteousness (right requirement) of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh (sinful self), but after the Spirit.
For those who are after the flesh (sinful self) do mind (think about) the things of the flesh. But those who are after the Spirit, the things of the Spirit.
For to be carnally (ruled by the sinful self) minded is death. But to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
Because the carnal (ruled by the sinful self) mind is enmity (hate) against God. For it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be.
So then those who are in the flesh (sinful self) cannot please God.
But you are not in the flesh (sinful self), but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwells (lives) in you. Now if any man does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is none of His.
And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin. But the Spirit is life because of righteousness (being right with God).

But if the Spirit of Him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells (lives) in you, He who raised up Christ from the dead will also quicken (make alive) your mortal (that will die) bodies by His Spirit who dwells (lives) in you.
So, brothers, we are debtors (we owe something), not to the flesh (sinful self), to live after the flesh.
For if you live after the flesh (sinful self), you will die. But if you through the Spirit do mortify (put to death) the deeds of the body, you will live.
For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.
For you have not received the spirit of bondage (slavery) again to fear. But you have received the Spirit of adoption (being made God's children), by which we cry: Abba, Father.
The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God.
And if children, then heirs: heirs of God, and joint-heirs (sharing heirs) with Christ. If so be that we suffer with Him, that we may be also glorified together.
For I reckon (count) that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which will be revealed (shown) in us.
For the earnest expectation (eager waiting) of the creature (creation) waits for the manifestation (showing) of the sons of God.
For the creature (creation) was made subject to vanity (emptiness), not willingly, but by reason of Him who has subjected the same in hope.
Because the creature (creation) itself also will be delivered (set free) from the bondage (slavery) of corruption (decay) into the glorious liberty (freedom) of the children of God.
For we know that the whole creation groans and travails (has pain like giving birth) together until now.

And not only they, but ourselves also, who have the firstfruits (first part) of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves. We wait for the adoption (being made God's children), that is, the redemption (being bought back and set free) of our body.
For we are saved by hope. But hope that is seen is not hope. For what a man sees, why does he yet hope for?
But if we hope for that we see not, then do we with patience wait for it.

Likewise the Spirit also helps our infirmities (weaknesses). For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought. But the Spirit Himself makes intercession (prays to God) for us with groanings which cannot be uttered (put into words).
And He who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because He makes intercession (prays to God) for the saints (holy people) according to the will of God.
And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose (plan).

For whom God did foreknow (know ahead of time), He also did predestinate (choose ahead of time) to be conformed to (made like) the image of His Son, that He might be the firstborn among many brothers.
Moreover whom He did predestinate (choose ahead of time), them He also called. And whom He called, them He also justified (made right with God). And whom He justified, them He also glorified.
What shall we then say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
He who spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all, how will He not with Him also freely give us all things?
Who will lay any thing to the charge of (accuse) God's elect (chosen people)? It is God who justifies (makes right with God).
Who is he who condemns (judges guilty)? It is Christ who died, yes rather, who is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also makes intercession (prays to God) for us.
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will tribulation (trouble), or distress, or persecution (being attacked for faith), or famine (no food), or nakedness, or peril (danger), or sword?
As it is written: For Your sake we are killed all the day long. We are accounted (counted) as sheep for the slaughter.
No, in all these things we are more than conquerors (winners) through Him who loved us.
For I am persuaded (sure), that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities (rulers), nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature (created thing), will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

9.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit,
That I have great heaviness (sadness) and continual sorrow in my heart.
For I could wish that I myself were accursed (cut off) from Christ for my brothers, my kinsmen (relatives) according to the flesh,
Who are Israelites. To them belongs the adoption (being made God's children), and the glory, and the agreements, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises.
Theirs are the fathers, and from them as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.
Not as though the word of God has taken none effect (failed). For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel.
Neither, because they are the seed (family line) of Abraham, are they all children. But: In Isaac will your seed be called.
That is, those who are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God. But the children of the promise are counted for the seed (family line).
For this is the word of promise: At this time I will come, and Sara (Sarah) will have a son.
And not only this. But when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac,
For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election (choosing) might stand, not of works, but of Him who calls,
It was said to her: The elder will serve the younger.
As it is written: Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.
What shall we say then? Is there unrighteousness (wrong) with God? God forbid (no, never).
For He says to Moses: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion (deep pity) on whom I will have compassion.
So then it is not of the one who wills, nor of the one who runs, but of God who shows mercy.
For the scripture says to Pharaoh: Even for this same purpose have I raised you up, that I might show My power in you, and that My name might be declared (told) throughout all the earth.
So God has mercy on whom He will have mercy, and whom He will He hardens.
You will say then to me: Why does God yet find fault? For who has resisted (stood against) His will?
No but, O man, who are you who replies against God? Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it: Why have you made me like this?
Has not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel (pot) to honor, and another to dishonor?
What if God, willing to show His wrath (God's anger), and to make His power known, endured (put up) with much longsuffering (patience) the vessels of wrath fitted (ready) to destruction,
And that He might make known the riches of His glory on the vessels of mercy, which He had before prepared unto glory,
Even us, whom He has called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews)?
As He says also in Osee (Hosea): I will call them My people, which were not My people. And her beloved, which was not beloved.
And it will come to pass, that in the place where it was said to them: You are not My people, there they will be called the children of the living God.
Esaias (Isaiah) also cries about Israel: Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant (a small part) will be saved.
For He will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness (rightness). Because a short work will the Lord make upon the earth.

And as Esaias (Isaiah) said before: Except the Lord of Sabaoth (the Lord of all armies) had left us a seed (a few people), we would have been as Sodoma (Sodom), and been made like Gomorrha (Gomorrah).

What shall we say then? That the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), who did not follow after righteousness (being right with God), have attained (reached) to righteousness, even the righteousness which is of faith.
But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness (being right with God), has not attained (reached) to the law of righteousness.
Why? Because they did not seek it by faith, but as it were by the works of the law. For they stumbled at that stumblingstone (stone that makes people trip),
As it is written: Look, I lay in Sion (Zion) a stumblingstone (stone that makes people trip) and rock of offence. And whoever believes on Him will not be ashamed.

10.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Brothers, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.
For I bear them record (witness) that they have a zeal (strong desire) of God, but not according to knowledge.

For they, being ignorant (not knowing) of God's righteousness (way of being right with God), and going about to establish (set up) their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves to the righteousness of God.
For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness (being right with God) to every one who believes.
For Moses describes the righteousness which is of the law: That the man who does those things will live by them.
But the righteousness which is of faith speaks this way: Say not in your heart: Who will ascend (go up) into heaven? (That is, to bring Christ down from above.)
Or: Who will descend (go down) into the deep? (That is, to bring up Christ again from the dead.)
But what does it say? The word is near you, even in your mouth, and in your heart. That is, the word of faith, which we preach.
That if you will confess (say openly) with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and will believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
For with the heart man believes unto righteousness (being right with God). And with the mouth confession (saying it openly) is made unto salvation.
For the scripture says: Whoever believes on Him will not be ashamed.
For there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek. For the same Lord over all is rich unto all who call upon Him.
For whoever will call upon the name of the Lord will be saved.
How then will they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how will they believe in Him of whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without a preacher?
And how will they preach, unless they are sent? As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the gospel (good news) of peace, and bring glad tidings (good news) of good things.
But they have not all obeyed the gospel (good news). For Esaias (Isaiah) says: Lord, who has believed our report (message)?
So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
But I say: Have they not heard? Yes truly, their sound went into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
But I say: Did not Israel know? First Moses says: I will provoke you to jealousy by those who are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you.
But Esaias (Isaiah) is very bold, and says: I was found by those who did not seek Me. I was made manifest (shown) to those who did not ask after Me.
But to Israel He says: All day long I have stretched out My hands to a disobedient and gainsaying (arguing) people.

11.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: I say then: Has God cast away His people? God forbid (no, never). For I also am an Israelite, of the seed (family line) of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not cast away His people which He foreknew (knew ahead of time). Do you not know what the scripture says of Elias (Elijah)? How he makes intercession (prays) to God against Israel, saying:
Lord, they have killed Your prophets, and dug down Your altars. And I am left alone, and they seek my life.
But what does the answer of God say to him? I have reserved (kept) to Myself 7,000 men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.
Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant (a small part) according to the election (choosing) of grace.
And if by grace, then it is no more of works. Otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it is of works, then it is no more grace. Otherwise work is no more work.
What then? Israel has not obtained (gotten) that which he seeks for. But the election (chosen people) has obtained it, and the rest were blinded.
According as it is written: God has given them the spirit of slumber (sleepiness), eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, unto this day.
And David says: Let their table be made a snare (trap), and a trap, and a stumblingblock (something that makes people trip), and a recompence (payment) to them.
Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see, and bow down their back always.
I say then: Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid (no, never). But rather through their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), to provoke them to jealousy.
Now if the fall of them is the riches of the world, and the diminishing (loss) of them the riches of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), how much more their fulness?
For I speak to you Gentiles (people who are not Jews). Inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify (honor) my office (work),
If by any means I may provoke to emulation (make jealous) those who are my flesh (my own people), and might save some of them.
For if the casting away of them is the reconciling (bringing back to God) of the world, what will the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?
For if the firstfruit (first part) is holy, the lump is also holy. And if the root is holy, so are the branches.

And if some of the branches are broken off, and you, being a wild olive tree, were graffed in (joined in) among them, and with them partake of (share) the root and fatness (richness) of the olive tree,
Do not boast (brag) against the branches. But if you boast, you do not bear the root, but the root bears you.
You will say then: The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in (joined in).
Well. Because of unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by faith. Be not highminded (proud), but fear.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, take heed (be careful) lest He also does not spare you.
See then the goodness and severity (strictness) of God. On those who fell, severity (strictness). But toward you, goodness, if you continue in His goodness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.
And they also, if they do not abide (stay) still in unbelief, will be graffed in (joined in). For God is able to graff them in again.

For if you were cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and were graffed (joined) contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be graffed into their own olive tree?

For I would not, brothers, that you should be ignorant (not knowing) of this mystery (secret), lest you should be wise in your own conceits (own opinion): that blindness in part has happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) has come in.
And so all Israel will be saved. As it is written: There will come out of Sion (Zion) the Deliverer (Rescuer), and will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
For this is My agreement with them, when I will take away their sins.
As concerning the gospel (good news), they are enemies for your sakes. But as touching the election (choosing), they are beloved for the fathers' sakes.
For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance (God does not take them back).
For as you in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief,
Even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy.
For God has concluded (shut up) them all in unbelief, that He might have mercy upon all.
O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God. How unsearchable (too great to measure) are His judgments, and His ways past finding out.
For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counsellor (adviser)?
Or who has first given to Him, and it will be recompensed (paid back) to him again?
For of Him, and through Him, and to Him, are all things. To Him be glory for ever. Amen.

12.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: I beseech (beg) you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable (pleasing) to God, which is your reasonable service.

And be not conformed to (shaped by) this world. But be transformed (changed) by the renewing (making new) of your mind, that you may prove (test and know) what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.

For I say, through the grace given to me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think. But to think soberly (with a clear mind), according as God has dealt to every man the measure of faith.
For as we have many members (parts) in one body, and all members have not the same office (job),
So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.
Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us: whether prophecy (speaking God's message), let us prophesy according to the proportion (measure) of faith.
Or ministry (serving), let us wait on our ministering. Or the one who teaches, on teaching.

Or the one who exhorts (encourages), on exhortation (encouragement). The one who gives, let him do it with simplicity (an honest heart). The one who rules, with diligence (hard work). The one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
Let love be without dissimulation (pretending). Abhor (hate) that which is evil. Cleave (hold tight) to that which is good.
Be kindly affectioned (loving) one to another with brotherly love. In honor preferring (putting first) one another.
Not slothful (lazy) in business. Fervent (on fire) in spirit. Serving the Lord.
Rejoicing in hope. Patient in tribulation (trouble). Continuing instant (always) in prayer.
Distributing (sharing) to the necessity of saints (holy people). Given to hospitality (welcoming strangers).
Bless those who persecute (attack) you. Bless, and curse not.
Rejoice with those who do rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to (be friends with) men of low estate (position). Be not wise in your own conceits (own opinion).
Recompense (pay back) to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.
If it be possible, as much as lies in you, live peaceably with all men.
Dearly beloved, avenge (pay back) not yourselves, but rather give place to wrath (God's anger). For it is written: Vengeance (paying back) is Mine. I will repay, says the Lord.
So if your enemy hunger, feed him. If he thirst, give him drink. For in so doing you will heap coals of fire on his head (make him feel ashamed).
Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Let every soul be subject (submit) to the higher powers (rulers). For there is no power but of God. The powers that be are ordained (set up) of God.
So whoever resists (stands against) the power, resists the ordinance (order) of God. And those who resist will receive to themselves damnation (being condemned).
For rulers are not a terror to good works (the good things we do), but to the evil. Will you then not be afraid of the power? Do what is good, and you will have praise of the same.

For he is the minister (servant) of God to you for good. But if you do what is evil, be afraid. For he does not bear the sword in vain (for nothing). For he is the minister (servant) of God, a revenger (one who pays back) to execute wrath (anger) upon the one who does evil.
So you must needs (must) be subject (submit), not only for wrath (punishment), but also for conscience sake.
For this cause pay also tribute (taxes). For they are God's ministers (servants), attending continually upon this very thing.
Render (give) therefore to all their dues: tribute (taxes) to whom tribute is due. Custom (fees) to whom custom. Fear to whom fear. Honor to whom honor.
Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For the one who loves another has fulfilled the law.

For this: You will not commit adultery (sex outside marriage). You will not kill. You will not steal. You will not bear false witness (lie about others). You will not covet (want what belongs to others). And if there is any other commandment, it is briefly comprehended (summed up) in this saying, namely: You will love your neighbor as yourself.
Love works no ill to his neighbor. So love is the fulfilling of the law.
And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep. For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.
The night is far spent (almost over), the day is at hand (near). So let us cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.
Let us walk honestly, as in the day. Not in rioting (wild parties) and drunkenness, not in chambering (sexual sin) and wantonness (shameful living), not in strife (fighting) and envying (jealousy).
But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision (plans) for the flesh (sinful self), to fulfil the lusts (wrong desires) of it.

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: Him who is weak in the faith receive, but not to doubtful disputations (arguments about opinions).
For one believes that he may eat all things. Another, who is weak, eats herbs (vegetables).
Let not the one who eats despise (look down on) the one who does not eat. And let not the one who does not eat judge the one who eats. For God has received him.
Who are you who judges another man's servant? To his own master he stands or falls. Yes, he will be held up. For God is able to make him stand.
One man esteems (honors) one day above another. Another esteems every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded (sure) in his own mind.

The one who regards (honors) the day, regards it unto the Lord. And the one who does not regard the day, to the Lord he does not regard it. The one who eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks. And the one who does not eat, to the Lord he does not eat, and gives God thanks.
For none of us lives to himself, and no man dies to himself.
For whether we live, we live unto the Lord. And whether we die, we die unto the Lord. Whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's.
For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived (lived again), that He might be Lord both of the dead and living.
But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you set at nought (look down on) your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
For it is written: As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to Me, and every tongue will confess (say openly) to God.
So then every one of us will give account of himself to God.
So let us not judge one another any more. But judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock (something that makes people trip) or an occasion to fall in his brother's way.
I know, and am persuaded (sure) by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself. But to the one who esteems (thinks) any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
But if your brother is grieved (hurt) with your meat (food), now you do not walk charitably (in love). Do not destroy him with your meat (food), for whom Christ died.
So let not your good be evil spoken of.
For the kingdom of God is not meat (food) and drink, but righteousness (being right with God), and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
For the one who in these things serves Christ is acceptable to God, and approved of men.
So let us follow after the things which make for peace, and things with which one may edify (build up) another.
For meat (food) do not destroy the work of God. All things indeed are pure. But it is evil for that man who eats with offence (causing others to fall).
It is good neither to eat flesh (meat), nor to drink wine, nor any thing by which your brother stumbles, or is offended (falls into sin), or is made weak.
Have you faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is the one who does not condemn (judge guilty) himself in that thing which he allows.
And the one who doubts is damned (condemned) if he eats, because he does not eat of faith. For whatever is not of faith is sin.

15.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: We then who are strong ought to bear the infirmities (weaknesses) of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
Let every one of us please his neighbor for his good to edification (building up).
For even Christ did not please Himself. But, as it is written: The reproaches (insults) of those who reproached You fell on Me.
For whatever things were written before were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
Now the God of patience and consolation (comfort) grant (give) you to be likeminded (agree) one toward another according to Christ Jesus,
That you may with one mind and one mouth glorify (praise) God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So receive one another, as Christ also received us to the glory of God.
Now I say that Jesus Christ was a minister (servant) of the circumcision (the Jews) for the truth of God, to confirm (make sure) the promises made to the fathers,
And that the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) might glorify (praise) God for His mercy. As it is written: For this cause I will confess (praise) You among the Gentiles, and sing to Your name.
And again He says: Rejoice, you Gentiles (people who are not Jews), with His people.
And again: Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles (people who are not Jews). And laud (praise) Him, all you people.
And again, Esaias (Isaiah) says: There will be a root of Jesse, and He who will rise to reign (rule) over the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). In Him will the Gentiles trust.
Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound (overflow) in hope, through the power of the Holy Spirit.
And I myself also am persuaded (sure) about you, my brothers, that you also are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish (warn) one another.
Nevertheless, brothers, I have written the more boldly to you in some sort (in some parts), as putting you in mind (reminding you), because of the grace that is given to me of God,

That I should be the minister (servant) of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), ministering the gospel (good news) of God. So the offering up of the Gentiles might be acceptable, being sanctified (made holy) by the Holy Spirit.
So I have reason to glory (rejoice) through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain (belong) to God.
For I will not dare to speak of any of those things which Christ has not done by me, to make the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) obedient, by word and deed,
Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem, and round about (all around) unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel (good news) of Christ.
Yes, so have I strived to preach the gospel (good news), not where Christ was named, lest I should build upon another man's foundation.
But as it is written: To whom He was not spoken of, they will see. And those who have not heard will understand.
For this cause also I have been much hindered (stopped) from coming to you.
But now having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come to you,
Whenever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you. For I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way there by you, if first I am somewhat filled with your company.
But now I go to Jerusalem to minister (serve) to the saints (holy people).
For it has pleased those of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution (gift) for the poor saints (holy people) who are at Jerusalem.

It has pleased them truly. And they are their debtors (they owe them). For if the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) have been made partakers (sharers) of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister (help) to them in carnal (earthly) things.
So when I have performed (finished) this, and have sealed (safely given) to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.
And I am sure that, when I come to you, I will come in the fulness of the blessing of the gospel (good news) of Christ.
Now I beg you, brothers, for the Lord Jesus Christ's sake, and for the love of the Spirit, that you strive together with me in your prayers to God for me,
That I may be delivered (rescued) from those who do not believe in Judea. And that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints (holy people).
That I may come to you with joy by the will of God, and may with you be refreshed.
Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

16.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was looser than the KJV), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: I commend (recommend) to you Phebe our sister, who is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea,

That you receive her in the Lord, as becomes (is right for) saints (holy people). And that you assist her in whatever business she has need of you. For she has been a succourer (helper) of many, and of myself also.
Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus,
Who have for my life laid down their own necks (risked their lives). To them not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute (greet) my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits (first believer) of Achaia unto Christ.
Greet Mary, who bestowed (gave) much labor (hard work) on us.
Salute (greet) Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen (relatives), and my fellowprisoners, who are of note (well known) among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.
Salute (greet) Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
Salute (greet) Apelles approved in Christ. Salute those who are of Aristobulus' household (family).
Salute (greet) Herodion my kinsman (relative). Greet those who are of the household (family) of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
Salute (greet) Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labor (work hard) in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, who labored much in the Lord.
Salute (greet) Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
Salute (greet) Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers who are with them.
Salute (greet) Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints (holy people) who are with them.
Salute (greet) one another with a holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute (greet) you.
Now I beg you, brothers, mark (watch out for) those who cause divisions and offences (stumbling) contrary to (against) the doctrine (teaching) which you have learned. And avoid them.
For those who are such do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly. By good words and fair speeches (smooth talk) they deceive (trick) the hearts of the simple (people who trust easily).
For your obedience has come abroad (become known) to all men. So I am glad on your behalf. But yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple (innocent) concerning evil.
And the God of peace will bruise (crush) Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
Timothy my workfellow, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen (relatives), salute (greet) you.
I Tertius, who wrote this epistle (letter), salute (greet) you in the Lord.
Gaius my host, and of the whole church, salutes (greets) you. Erastus the chamberlain (treasurer) of the city salutes you, and Quartus a brother.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

Now to Him who is of power to stablish (make strong) you according to my gospel (good news), and the preaching of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation (showing) of the mystery (secret), which was kept secret since the world began,
But now is made manifest (shown), and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith:
To God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
